name: Alfred Workflows
description: Alfred Workflows extend Alfred's macOS productivity app with configurable triggers, inputs, actions, automation tasks, scripts, and outputs. Powerpack users can build or import workflows and discover community-maintained integrations through the Alfred Gallery.
agentUseSummary: Alfred Workflows cannot yet be connected to Relay agents because they execute through an installed Mac app with broad local permissions and arbitrary-script authority, while Alfred's external triggers, Remote companion, Gallery, and optional settings sync do not provide a bounded provider-authenticated cloud API contract.

blocked.label: Connect Alfred Workflows
blocked.description: Relay does not present an Alfred Powerpack license, installed application, workflow library, sync folder, Gallery state, or macOS security permission as a Railway API connection.

blocked.label: Control local Alfred workflows
blocked.description: Relay does not invoke alfred URL handlers, AppleScript, JavaScript for Automation, Alfred Remote triggers, local workflow objects, environment variables, preferences, or private application-support files.

blocked.label: Install or update workflows
blocked.description: Relay does not discover, download, import, install, update, sign, or trust Gallery or third-party workflow packages, scripts, binaries, libraries, dependencies, or workflow-supplied API credentials.

blocked.label: Execute workflow automation
blocked.description: Scripts, commands, files, folders, clipboard data, contacts, browsers, applications, windows, images, URLs, text, and other workflow effects remain unavailable until Relay ships explicit Mac-local authority and bounded approvals.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Relay ships a separately disclosed, user-authorized Mac-local connector with an immutable reviewed workflow allowlist and no arbitrary-code or unbounded local-data surface.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay does not silently bridge OpenClaw to Alfred's installed app, Powerpack workflows, Gallery packages, local triggers, scripts, permissions, preferences, or private data.
Relay does not silently bridge Hermes to Alfred's installed app, Powerpack workflows, Gallery packages, local triggers, scripts, permissions, preferences, or private data.

providerSetup.blocker: Alfred Workflows are configured and executed through Alfred on the user's Mac. Their objects can open files and URLs, operate on local text and contacts, run Automation Tasks, and execute commands through built-in or arbitrary external interpreters. Alfred documents macOS Accessibility, Full Disk Access, Contacts, Automation, and sometimes Input Monitoring permissions for relevant local behavior. External Triggers are local AppleScript, JavaScript for Automation, or alfred URL-handler calls into a specified installed workflow, and Alfred Remote is a companion trigger for that same local workflow authority. The Gallery provides signed, reviewed distribution rather than remote execution; packaged binaries and libraries may not be fully inspectable, and community workflows can require paths, packages, API keys, subscriptions, or other dependencies. Optional preferences sync stores a locally available settings package at a user-selected cloud location. These surfaces do not establish a bounded Alfred cloud API, OAuth grant, webhook, or remote MCP contract, and Relay's current Marketplace runtime excludes local-app command execution.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request a Powerpack license, workflow-supplied API key, sync credential, preference folder, application permission, workflow package, bundle identifier, trigger identifier, variable, or local state; install or update workflows; invoke alfred URLs, AppleScript, JavaScript for Automation, Alfred Remote, scripts, or commands; inspect local preferences; automate the app UI; or show Connect. Reconsider after Relay ships a disclosed Mac-local connector that verifies Alfred, Powerpack, and the exact signed workflow are present; pins immutable reviewed bundle and action identifiers; exposes typed bounded inputs and outputs; rejects arbitrary scripts, binaries, dependencies, and dynamic downloads; obtains least-privilege permissions; requires approval for external effects; redacts secrets; audits calls; and supports revocation.

evidence.supports: Alfred describes Powerpack workflows launched by hotkey, keyword, or Alfred Remote and points users to a community workflow ecosystem and the official Alfred Gallery.
Alfred documents locally configured or imported workflows composed from triggers, inputs, actions, automation tasks, utilities, outputs, and user-interface objects.
Alfred documents Accessibility, Full Disk Access, Contacts, Automation, and sometimes Input Monitoring permissions used for local search, snippets, scripts, commands, and application control.
Alfred documents External Triggers as calls into an installed workflow through AppleScript, JavaScript for Automation, or a local alfred URL containing workflow and trigger identifiers.
Alfred's official Run Script action executes commands directly in macOS and supports built-in interpreters or external scripts selected by path or shebang.

The Alfred Gallery documents automated and manual checks, signed workflow installation and updates, public source for review, and warnings where packaged binaries or libraries prevent full inspection.
